# Typeform vs Formbricks (2026)

## Overview
Typeform and Formbricks are both online form and survey tools used to collect data from users. This comparison is beneficial for individuals and businesses looking to switch from a proprietary, cloud-based solution like Typeform to a self-hosted, open-source alternative like Formbricks. The core use case for both tools is data collection, and the key reason someone would switch is to have more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Typeform has a monthly subscription fee, while Formbricks is free and open-source.
* Data ownership: Formbricks allows users to have full ownership and control over their data, while Typeform stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Typeform has a simpler setup process, while Formbricks requires more technical expertise to self-host.
* Scalability: Formbricks can be more scalable than Typeform, as users can host it on their own servers.
* Integration difference: Formbricks has a more limited range of integrations with third-party tools compared to Typeform.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Typeform | Formbricks |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $25-$83/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $25-$40/month (billed annually) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $50-$100/month (billed annually) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Typeform
* Easy to use and set up
* Wide range of integrations with third-party tools
* Good customer support
* Limited control over data
* Can be expensive for large teams
### Formbricks
* Free and open-source
* Self-hosted option for full data control
* Highly customizable
* Limited integrations with third-party tools
* Requires technical expertise to set up

## When to Choose Each
Typeform is a good choice for small to medium-sized teams who need a simple, easy-to-use form and survey tool with a wide range of integrations. It's also a good option for those who don't mind paying a monthly subscription fee and don't require full control over their data. 
Formbricks, on the other hand, is a good choice for larger teams or organizations who require full control over their data and are willing to invest time and resources into setting up and customizing the tool. It's also a good option for those who are looking for a free, open-source solution and have the technical expertise to self-host.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Typeform data in CSV or JSON format.
2. Set up a Formbricks instance on your own server or use a hosting service.
3. Use the Formbricks import tool to import your Typeform data.
4. Customize and configure Formbricks to fit your needs.
5. Test and verify that your forms and surveys are working as expected.

## Our Take
Formbricks is still a relatively new tool, and while it shows promise, it may not be production-ready for most users right now. One specific technical limitation worth knowing before switching is that Formbricks has limited support for advanced conditional logic and branching.
However, for teams who value data control and customization, and are willing to invest time and resources into setting up and maintaining the tool, Formbricks is a good choice. We recommend switching to Formbricks if you're a technically savvy team with specific customization needs, but sticking with Typeform if you prioritize ease of use and a wide range of integrations.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams with simple form needs who want to save money
* Medium-sized teams who require more control over their data
* Large teams with technical expertise who need high customization
* Organizations with strict data privacy requirements
* Developers who want to self-host and customize their form tool

## FAQ
### Can I use Formbricks for free?
Yes, Formbricks is free and open-source, and you can self-host it on your own server.
### Is Formbricks as easy to use as Typeform?
No, Formbricks requires more technical expertise to set up and customize.
### Can I integrate Formbricks with other tools?
Formbricks has limited integrations with third-party tools, but it's highly customizable, so you can build your own integrations.
### Is my data safe with Formbricks?
Yes, with Formbricks, you have full control over your data, and it's stored on your own server.
### Can I migrate my Typeform data to Formbricks?
Yes, you can export your Typeform data in CSV or JSON format and import it into Formbricks.

title: Miro vs Excalidraw

# Miro vs Excalidraw (2026)

## Overview
Miro and Excalidraw are two popular tools used for collaborative whiteboarding and visual project management. This comparison benefits teams and individuals looking for a platform to enhance their remote collaboration and creativity. A key reason someone would switch from Miro to Excalidraw is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Miro offers a free plan and several paid plans, while Excalidraw is completely free.
* Data ownership: Excalidraw allows users to self-host their data, giving them full control and ownership, whereas Miro stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup complexity: Miro has a more straightforward setup process, while Excalidraw requires more technical expertise, especially for self-hosting.
* Scalability: Miro is designed to handle large teams and enterprises, while Excalidraw is better suited for smaller teams and individuals.
* Integration difference: Miro has a more extensive library of integrations with third-party tools, including Google Drive and Trello, while Excalidraw has limited integrations.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Miro | Excalidraw |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $8-$16/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $400-$800/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,600-$3,200/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Miro:**
* Pros:
	+ User-friendly interface
	+ Extensive integration library
	+ Scalable for large teams
	+ Robust collaboration features
* Cons:
	+ Limited control over data
	+ Can be expensive for large teams
	+ Limited customization options
**Excalidraw:**
* Pros:
	+ Completely free
	+ Self-hosting option for data control
	+ Lightweight and fast
	+ Open-source community
* Cons:
	+ Limited integrations
	+ Steeper learning curve
	+ Limited support for large teams
	+ Limited mobile support

## When to Choose Each
Miro is suitable for large teams and enterprises that require a robust and scalable collaboration platform with a wide range of integrations. It is ideal for teams that prioritize ease of use and are willing to pay for the convenience. On the other hand, Excalidraw is perfect for small teams, individuals, and those who value data control and customization. It is ideal for teams that are technically inclined and want a free, self-hosted solution.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Miro boards as JSON files.
2. Use the Excalidraw import tool to convert the JSON files into Excalidraw format.
3. Set up your Excalidraw server and configure the necessary settings.
4. Invite your team members to join the Excalidraw platform and start collaborating.
5. Update any integrations or workflows to work with Excalidraw.

## Our Take
Excalidraw is not yet production-ready for most users, as it lacks some of the polish and features of Miro. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Excalidraw has limited support for mobile devices, which may be a concern for teams that collaborate on-the-go. However, for teams that value data control and customization, Excalidraw is a great option, and we recommend switching to Excalidraw if you are a small team or individual with basic collaboration needs.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) who do not need extensive integrations
* Individuals who value data control and customization
* Teams that are technically inclined and can handle self-hosting
* Teams that prioritize cost savings and do not need advanced features
* Teams that do not require mobile support

## FAQ
### Can I use Excalidraw for large teams?
No, Excalidraw is not yet suitable for large teams, as it lacks the scalability and features of Miro.
### Is Excalidraw completely free?
Yes, Excalidraw is completely free, with no costs or fees associated with using the platform.
### Can I self-host Excalidraw?
Yes, Excalidraw offers a self-hosting option, giving users full control over their data and servers.
### Does Excalidraw have mobile support?
No, Excalidraw has limited support for mobile devices, which may be a concern for teams that collaborate on-the-go.
### Can I import my Miro boards into Excalidraw?
Yes, Excalidraw offers an import tool that allows you to convert your Miro boards into Excalidraw format.

title: Netlify vs Coolify
comparison_markdown:
# Netlify vs Coolify

## Overview

Popular platform for deploying and hosting web apps and static sites. is a popular proprietary tool in the developer-tools space. Coolify is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Netlify costs Free / $19-$99/month; Coolify is Free (self-hosted)
- **License**: Netlify is Proprietary; Coolify is Apache 2.0
- **Data ownership**: Coolify can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Coolify eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Coolify has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Netlify | Coolify |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $19-$99/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Netlify

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Coolify

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [coollabsio/coolify](https://github.com/coollabsio/coolify) * ~35k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Netlify if:** Netlify is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Coolify if:** Coolify is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Netlify in its standard export format, review Coolify import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Coolify is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Netlify tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Coolify instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Netlify, switching to self-hosted Coolify will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Netlify until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Netlify paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Coolify free to use?
Yes. Coolify is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Netlify to Coolify?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Netlify data, follow the Coolify import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Coolify get regular updates?
Yes. Coolify has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Coolify without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Coolify development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced July 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Netlify](https://netlify.com) and [Coolify](https://coolify.io) before making decisions.*
meta_description: Coolify is a free, self-hosted alternative to Netlify. Compare pricing, features, and migration steps. See full comparison.

* High degree of customizability
* Open-source community
